Inside the Mitochondria
¨The Preparatory (prep) Reaction¤Connects glycolysis to the citric acid cycle¤End product of glycolysis, pyruvate, enters the mitochondrial matrix¤Pyruvate is converted to a 2-carbon acetyl groupnAttached to Coenzyme A to form acetyl-CoAnElectrons are picked up (as hydrogen atom) by NAD+nCO2is released and transported out of mitochondria into the cytoplasm
explanation: The preparatory (prep) reaction connects glycolysis to the citric acid cycle. The end product of glycolysis, pyruvate, enters the mitochondrial matrix. There, pyruvate is converted into a 2-carbon acetyl group and attached to Coenzyme A, forming acetyl-CoA. During this oxidation step, electrons are picked up (as hydrogen atoms) by NAD+ to form NADH, and carbon dioxide (CO2) is released, eventually diffusing out of the mitochondria into the cytoplasm.

questions.q: What is the end product of the preparatory reaction that enters the Citric Acid Cycle?
questions.exp: The notes state that pyruvate is converted to a '2-carbon acetyl group' and 'Attached to Coenzyme A to form acetyl-CoA', connecting glycolysis to the citric acid cycle.

questions.q: What by-product is released and transported out of the mitochondria during the preparatory reaction?
questions.exp: The notes state: 'CO2 is released and transported out of mitochondria into the cytoplasm.'
